sections.skill: Plan a learning route and portfolio for a stated goal

questions.prompt: What is a learning route?

choices.text: A plan from where you are to a stated goal
A list of every AI course that exists

questions.correct_answer: A plan from where you are to a stated goal
questions.intro: A LEARNING ROUTE is a plan from where you are to a stated GOAL, such as "help my nonprofit use AI tools safely" or "get an entry-level data analysis role." Work backward: what tasks does the goal involve, what skills do those tasks need, and which free or low-cost resources teach them? A PORTFOLIO is a collection of evidence of what you can do: small projects, write-ups explaining your choices, and tests showing your work is correct. Match portfolio pieces to the goal. No course, certificate or portfolio GUARANTEES a job, but clear evidence helps.

questions.intro: Use four steps. (1) GOAL: state it clearly. (2) TASKS: list what someone reaching that goal does. (3) SKILLS: list what each task requires. (4) EVIDENCE: plan a small project that shows each key skill. Example goal: "Help my club use AI to draft newsletters safely." Tasks: draft, check facts, protect member privacy. Skills: prompting, fact-checking, privacy basics. Evidence: a sample newsletter with notes on what was checked and what personal information was left out.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Make portfolios honest and keep routes current

questions.prompt: Should a portfolio say where AI help was used?

choices.text: Yes; be honest about what you did
No, because mentioning AI help always makes employers think the work has no value at all

questions.correct_answer: Yes; be honest about what you did
questions.intro: Portfolios are stronger when they are honest and specific. Say what you did yourself and where you used AI help; employers and teachers increasingly ask. Show a problem, your approach, your checks and the result, including what did not work. Keep projects small enough to finish. Update the route as you learn: if a skill turns out to matter more than you expected, adjust, and ask people working in the field what evidence they value.

questions.prompt: Which write-up is strongest?

choices.text: Problem, approach, checks, result and what did not work
Only the final result, presented as perfect, with no mention of any problems along the way
